subsystems.name: Transmitter modules (Alice and Bob)
subsystems.role: generate phase-randomised weak coherent pulses with randomly chosen basis and intensity.

subsystems.name: Phase and frequency stabilisation
subsystems.role: keep the two independent lasers coherent so their photons can interfere at the midpoint.
parts: optical phase-locked loop or reference laser

subsystems.name: Quantum channel
subsystems.role: carry photons from each transmitter to the midpoint with minimal loss and polarisation drift.
parts: polarisation-maintaining fibre or active polarisation compensation

subsystems.name: Midpoint measurement station (Charlie)
subsystems.role: interfere the two incoming pulses and announce detection events.
parts: single-photon detectors, such as superconducting nanowire detectors

subsystems.name: Post-processing and key management
subsystems.role: turn detection announcements into a secret key.

buildSteps.title: Choose link topology and midpoint site
buildSteps.detail: Measure fibre loss along the route and place the midpoint station so the two paths have comparable or well-characterised loss.

buildSteps.title: Build transmitter units
buildSteps.detail: Integrate narrow-linewidth lasers, phase and intensity modulators, and random number generators for basis and intensity choices; test decoy-state modulation.

buildSteps.title: Implement phase locking
buildSteps.detail: Connect a reference path or optical phase-locked loops between each transmitter and the midpoint, then demonstrate stable interference over minutes.

buildSteps.title: Install midpoint detector station
buildSteps.detail: Mount the interferometer and single-photon detectors in a cryostat or cooled enclosure, and calibrate timing and detection efficiency.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate interference visibility
buildSteps.detail: Send weak coherent pulses from both sides, scan their relative phase, and record coincidence counts to verify single-photon interference.

buildSteps.title: Run the protocol
buildSteps.detail: Transmit pulses with randomised phases, bases and intensities; the midpoint announces detections; senders post-select on matching basis and intensity.

buildSteps.title: Post-process the detections
buildSteps.detail: Sift the events, correct errors, bound eavesdropper information with decoy-state analysis, and apply privacy amplification to produce a key.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with encryptors
buildSteps.detail: Feed the keys to optical encryptors for data traffic, while monitoring key rate and quantum bit error rate.

prerequisites.tech: Single-photon detectors with high efficiency and low dark counts
prerequisites.why: the midpoint must register individual photons from both senders with low noise.

prerequisites.tech: Phase-stabilised fibre interferometry over tens of kilometres
prerequisites.why: independent photons only interfere if their relative phase is held steady.
it bounds how much information an eavesdropper could gain from weak coherent pulses.

prerequisites.tech: Classical authenticated channel and fast post-processing
prerequisites.why: senders and the midpoint must exchange basis, intensity and detection information without being spoofed.
